explanation.title: Spanish Negation: Expressing What Is Not

sections.subtitle: Basic Negation with NO
sections.content:
❌ BASIC NEGATION

Use NO placed directly before the verb

→ No hablo inglés (I don't speak English)
→ No quiero café (I don't want coffee)
→ No es fácil (It's not easy)

⚠️ NO is NEVER separated from verb
(Unlike English 'do not')

→ No tengo tiempo (I don't have time)
→ NO directly before verb

📍 With object pronouns:

NO comes BEFORE the pronoun:
→ No lo veo (I don't see it - NO before lo)
→ No me gusta (I don't like it - NO before me)

📍 In compound tenses:

NO goes before auxiliary:
→ No he comido (I haven't eaten)
→ No había terminado (He/She hadn't finished)

📍 With infinitives/gerunds:

NO can precede them:
→ Es importante no olvidar
(It's important not to forget)
→ No fumando es mejor
(Not smoking is better)

❓ In questions:

NO typically before verb:
→ ¿No vienes? (Aren't you coming?)
→ ¿No te gusta? (Don't you like it?)

✅ YES/NO answers:
→ Sí (yes)
→ No (no)

To emphasize: Sí, sí / No, no

💡 Agreement with negative:
→ No me gusta. A mí tampoco
(I don't like it. Me neither - use tampoco, not también)

sections.subtitle: Negative Words: NUNCA, NADIE, NADA, NINGUNO
sections.content:
❌ SPANISH NEGATIVE WORDS

• NUNCA/JAMÁS (never)
• NADIE (nobody/no one)
• NADA (nothing)
• NINGUNO/A (none/not any)
• TAMPOCO (neither/not either)
• NI (nor/not even)

📋 WORD ORDER RULE:

✅ Negative word BEFORE verb → do NOT use NO
→ Nunca como carne (I never eat meat)
→ Nadie vino (Nobody came)

✅ Negative word AFTER verb → USE NO before verb
→ No como nunca carne (I never eat meat)
→ No vino nadie (Nobody came)

Both patterns mean the same thing!
Position choice is stylistic.

💡 NUNCA vs JAMÁS:

Both mean 'never'
JAMÁS is stronger/more emphatic

→ Nunca he estado en París
(I've never been to Paris)

→ Jamás te olvidaré
(I'll NEVER forget you - stronger)

👤 NADIE (refers to people):

→ No veo a nadie
(I don't see anyone - personal 'a' used)
→ Nadie sabe (Nobody knows)

📦 NADA (refers to things):

→ No tengo nada
(I have nothing / I don't have anything)
→ Nada me importa
(Nothing matters to me)

sections.subtitle: NINGUNO & Double/Multiple Negatives
sections.content:
📍 NINGUNO/A (no, none, not any)

Agrees in gender
Drops -o before masculine singular nouns

→ No tengo ningún libro
(I don't have any book / I have no book)
→ ningún before masculine singular noun

→ No tengo ninguna idea
(I don't have any idea)
→ ninguna before feminine noun

→ Ninguno de ellos vino
(None of them came - ninguno as pronoun)

Plural forms (ningunos/ningunas) are rare; use singular

💪 DOUBLE/MULTIPLE NEGATIVES

⚠️ Unlike English where two negatives cancel,
Spanish uses multiple negatives to REINFORCE negation
They DON'T cancel!

→ No veo nunca a nadie
(I never see anyone)
→ Literally: I don't see never nobody
→ THREE negatives!

→ No quiero nada nunca
(I never want anything)
→ Literally: I don't want nothing never

→ No tengo nunca ningún problema
(I never have any problem)
→ Multiple negatives reinforce

→ Nadie dice nunca nada
(Nobody ever says anything)
→ Literally: Nobody says never nothing

💡 This is CORRECT and standard Spanish!
The more negatives, the stronger the negation.

📋 Common patterns:
• No...nunca (never)
• No...nadie (nobody)
• No...nada (nothing)
• No...ninguno (none/not any)
• No...tampoco (neither/not either)

All can be combined:
→ No veo nunca nada (I never see anything)

sections.subtitle: TAMPOCO & NI...NI Construction
sections.content:
🔄 TAMPOCO (neither/not either)

Negative counterpart of TAMBIÉN (also/too)
Used in negative contexts for agreement

→ No me gusta el café. A mí tampoco
(I don't like coffee. Me neither)

→ No voy. Yo tampoco
(I'm not going. Me neither)

→ Tampoco quiero ir
(I don't want to go either - before verb, no NO needed)

→ No quiero ir tampoco
(I don't want to go either - after verb, NO needed)

⚠️ Never use TAMBIÉN in negative contexts
Always use TAMPOCO

❌ WRONG: No me gusta también
✅ CORRECT: No me gusta tampoco / Tampoco me gusta

📍 NI...NI (neither...nor)

Coordinates negative elements

→ No tengo ni tiempo ni dinero
(I have neither time nor money)
(I don't have time nor money)

→ Ni Juan ni María vienen
(Neither Juan nor María is coming)
→ ni before each element, no NO when ni comes first

→ No come ni carne ni pescado
(He eats neither meat nor fish)

Can extend to more items:
→ No tengo ni tiempo, ni dinero, ni energía
(I have neither time, nor money, nor energy)

💡 NI alone = 'not even':

→ Ni lo intentó
(He didn't even try it)

→ Ni siquiera (not even - emphasis):
→ Ni siquiera lo miró
(He didn't even look at it)

sections.subtitle: SIN + Infinitive & Negative Infinitives
sections.content:
📍 SIN + INFINITIVE

Expresses 'without' doing something
A form of negation - expressing absence of action

→ Salió sin decir nada
(He left without saying anything)

→ Trabaja sin descansar
(He works without resting)

→ Vivo sin problemas
(I live without problems)

💡 Compare:
→ Sin comer bien, no puedes estudiar
(Without eating well, you can't study)

⚠️ SIN doesn't need to repeat negative words:
→ Sin nada (without anything - just one negative)

❌ NEGATIVE INFINITIVES

To negate infinitive directly, place NO before it:

→ Es mejor no hablar
(It's better not to talk)

→ Decidí no ir
(I decided not to go)

→ Prefiero no comer carne
(I prefer not to eat meat)

→ Es importante no olvidar
(It's important not to forget)

📋 NEGATIVE COMMANDS with infinitives (signs/instructions):

→ No fumar (No smoking)
→ No tocar (Do not touch)
→ No entrar (Do not enter)

These are common on signs

📍 NEGATING GERUNDS:

→ No fumando, vivirás más
(By not smoking, you'll live longer)

Past participles less common with direct negation

📋 PATTERN:
NO + infinitive/gerund for negative non-finite forms

sections.subtitle: Negative Polarity Items & Special Constructions
sections.content:
🔄 NEGATIVE POLARITY ITEMS (NPIs)

Words/expressions that typically appear in negative contexts or questions

⏰ TODAVÍA NO / AÚN NO (not yet):
→ Todavía no he comido
(I haven't eaten yet)
→ ¿Has terminado? Todavía no
(Have you finished? Not yet)

⏰ YA NO (no longer/not anymore):
→ Ya no vivo aquí
(I don't live here anymore / I no longer live here)
→ Ya no me gusta
(I don't like it anymore)

Contrast: YA (already) vs YA NO (no longer)

💪 NI SIQUIERA (not even) - emphatic:
→ Ni siquiera lo intentó
(He didn't even try it)
→ No tengo ni siquiera un euro
(I don't even have one euro)

❌ EN ABSOLUTO / PARA NADA (not at all):
Strong negation

→ ¿Te gusta? En absoluto
(Do you like it? Not at all)
→ No me gusta para nada
(I don't like it at all)

💬 EXPRESSIONS:
• Nada de nada (nothing at all - emphasis)
• Nunca jamás (never ever - double emphasis)
• Nadie de nadie (nobody at all)

❓ NEGATIVE QUESTIONS expecting positive answer:
→ ¿No quieres venir?
(Don't you want to come? - expecting 'yes')

Answer: Sí (yes) or No (no)

💡 RHETORICAL negatives:
→ No es nada del otro mundo
(It's nothing special - idiomatic)

questions.question: Where does NO go in a sentence?

answers.text: At the beginning of the sentence
At the end of the sentence

questions.hint: NO always goes directly before the verb: No hablo (I don't speak).

questions.question: 'No lo veo' - Where does NO go with object pronouns?

answers.text: Before the object pronoun (No lo veo)
After the object pronoun (Lo no veo)

questions.hint: NO comes before object pronouns: No LO veo (I don't see IT).

questions.question: 'Nunca como carne' vs 'No como nunca carne' - Which is correct?

answers.text: Both are correct (different word order, same meaning)
Only 'No como nunca carne' is correct

questions.hint: Both patterns work: Negative word BEFORE verb (no NO) or AFTER verb (with NO).

questions.question: 'Nadie vino' vs 'No vino nadie' - What's the pattern?

answers.text: Negative word before verb (no NO); after verb (add NO)

questions.hint: Pattern: Nadie (before) = no NO. No...nadie (after) = use NO.

questions.question: NUNCA vs JAMÁS - What's the difference?

answers.text: Both mean 'never'; jamás is stronger/more emphatic
Nunca is formal, jamás is informal
Nunca is past, jamás is future

questions.hint: Both = never. JAMÁS is more emphatic: Jamás te olvidaré (I'll NEVER forget you - strong).

questions.question: 'No veo a nadie' - Why the personal 'a'?

answers.text: NADIE refers to people, needs personal 'a'

questions.hint: NADIE (nobody) refers to people, so use personal A: No veo A nadie.

questions.question: 'No tengo nada' means...

answers.text: I have nothing / I don't have anything

questions.hint: NADA = nothing. No tengo nada = I don't have anything/nothing.

questions.question: 'No tengo ningún libro' - Why 'ningún' not 'ninguno'?

answers.text: Ninguno drops -o before masculine singular nouns

questions.hint: NINGUNO/ALGUNO/PRIMERO drop -O before masculine singular nouns: ningún libro.

questions.question: 'No veo nunca a nadie' - Is this correct Spanish?

answers.text: Yes - multiple negatives reinforce negation in Spanish

questions.hint: Spanish embraces multiple negatives - they reinforce, don't cancel. Perfectly correct!

questions.question: 'No quiero nada nunca' - How many negatives?

answers.text: Three negatives (no, nada, nunca) - all reinforcing

questions.hint: Count them: NO + NADA + NUNCA = 3 negatives, all reinforcing the negation.

questions.question: 'Nadie dice nunca nada' - Is this acceptable Spanish?
questions.hint: Nadie + nunca + nada = three negatives reinforcing. Standard Spanish!

questions.question: 'No me gusta el café. A mí ___' (también/tampoco)
questions.hint: In negative contexts, use TAMPOCO (not también). A mí tampoco = Me neither.

questions.question: 'Tampoco quiero ir' vs 'No quiero ir tampoco' - Both correct?

answers.text: Yes - tampoco before verb (no NO) or after verb (with NO)

questions.hint: Same pattern as other negatives: before verb = no NO, after verb = use NO.

questions.question: 'No tengo ni tiempo ni dinero' means...

answers.text: I have neither time nor money
I have either time or money
I have both time and money
I have only time, not money

questions.hint: NI...NI = neither...nor. I have NEITHER time NOR money.

questions.question: 'Ni Juan ni María vienen' - Why no NO before ni?

answers.text: When ni comes before verb, NO is not needed

questions.hint: When NI starts the sentence (before verb), no NO needed. Ni Juan ni María = Neither Juan nor María.

questions.question: 'Ni siquiera lo intentó' means...

answers.text: He didn't even try it (emphatic negative)

questions.hint: NI SIQUIERA = not even (emphatic). He didn't EVEN try it.

questions.question: 'Salió sin decir nada' means...

answers.text: He left saying nothing is important

questions.hint: SIN + infinitive = without doing. Salió sin decir = left without saying.

questions.question: 'Es mejor no hablar' - Where does NO go with infinitives?

answers.text: Before the infinitive (no hablar = not to talk)
NO cannot be used with infinitives

questions.hint: To negate infinitives, place NO before them: NO hablar = not to talk.

questions.question: 'Todavía no he comido' means...
questions.hint: TODAVÍA NO / AÚN NO = not yet. I haven't eaten YET.

questions.question: 'Ya no vivo aquí' means...

answers.text: I don't live here anymore / I no longer live here

questions.hint: YA NO = no longer/not anymore. I NO LONGER live here.

questions.question: 'Ya' vs 'Ya no' - What's the difference?

answers.text: Ya = already; Ya no = no longer/not anymore
Ya is past, Ya no is future

questions.hint: YA = already (positive). YA NO = no longer/not anymore (negative change of state).

questions.question: 'No me gusta para nada' means...

answers.text: I don't like it at all (emphatic negative)

questions.hint: PARA NADA / EN ABSOLUTO = not at all (emphatic). I don't like it AT ALL.

questions.question: 'Nunca jamás' - Why use both?
questions.hint: NUNCA JAMÁS = never ever (double negative for emphasis, very strong).

questions.question: '¿No quieres venir?' expecting 'yes' - How to answer affirmatively?

answers.text: Sí (yes - answer based on reality, not question form)

questions.hint: Answer based on reality/meaning, not question form. If 'yes I want', say SÍ.
